records.issue_text: absolutize_urls does not rewrite document-relative URLs such as images/a.png or ../page, causing them to resolve against the Discourse URL instead of the source article
records.rationale: The absolutize_urls method in topic_embed.rb only handles URLs that start_with?('/'), meaning it only converts root-relative URLs (like '/hello' or '/images/wat.jpg'). Document-relative URLs without a leading slash (like 'images/a.png' or '../page') would not be matched by the start_with?('/') condition and would remain unchanged, causing them to resolve incorrectly against the Discourse base URL

records.issue_text: absolutize_urls incorrectly treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative, rewriting them to paths on the source host
records.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in topic_embed.rb, it checks if href/src start_with?('/') and then prepends the prefix. Protocol-relative URLs like '//example.com/image.jpg' also start with '/', so they would be incorrectly rewritten to 'http://eviltrout.com//example.com/image.jpg' instead of being left alone. This is a real bug in the URL handling logic.

records.issue_text: embed_url uses varchar(255) despite accepting unbounded URLs, causing longer article URLs to fail asynchronously during insertion
records.rationale: The migration in db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb creates embed_url as 't.string :embed_url, null: false' which defaults to varchar(255) in Rails. The code accepts URLs from external sources (RSS feeds, user input) without length validation. URLs longer than 255 characters would cause database insertion failures.
